data.name: ThemeTooltip
data.value: Switch between automatic, light and dark

data.name: SelectAnApplication
data.value: Select an application above to see its connections.

data.name: RuleExecutableChanged
data.value: ⚠ The program has changed since this rule was created.

data.name: HostsIntro
data.value: Destinations ranked by traffic, across every application. The list above answers what one program is doing; this answers it from the other end — a host several unrelated programs all talk to is worth a look. Loopback is excluded.

data.name: NothingBlocked
data.value: Nothing is blocked. Use "Block an app…" or select an application above.

data.name: CaptureIntro
data.value: Keyhole launches the application with SSLKEYLOGFILE set for that process only, and records its packets alongside. The capture carries its own TLS keys, so Wireshark opens it decrypted with nothing to configure. Applications on Windows' own TLS stack write no keys and stay encrypted.

data.name: GetNpcapTooltip
data.value: Downloads the installer from npcap.com and verifies its signature before running it. Keyhole does not redistribute Npcap.

data.name: RequestsTooltip
data.value: Decrypts the capture with this session's own TLS keys and lists what the application asked for.

data.name: WiresharkTooltip
data.value: Opens the capture in Wireshark. The TLS keys are inside the file, so no keylog path needs setting.

data.name: SettingsCloseToTray
data.value: Close to the tray instead of exiting

data.name: SettingsStartWithWindows
data.value: Start Keyhole when I sign in

data.name: SettingsPcapLimitNote
data.value: A browser session can produce hundreds of megabytes in minutes. At the limit the packet recording stops and says so; the session keeps running and keeps collecting TLS keys. Takes effect for captures started after the service restarts.

data.name: SettingsDataNote
data.value: Flow history, rules and captures live in %ProgramData%\Keyhole. A capture folder holds the recorded packets and the TLS keys that decrypt them, in one place — treat it as sensitive as the traffic itself.

data.name: StatusServiceSilent
data.value: Service did not answer within 5 seconds.

data.name: CapabilityNotElevated
data.value: The service is not elevated, so {0} are unavailable. Connection monitoring still works.

data.name: ReasonNotElevated
data.value: The service is not running with administrator rights.

data.name: ReasonEtwUnavailable
data.value: The trace session could not be started, so traffic volumes read zero.

data.name: ReasonFirewallUnreachable
data.value: Windows Firewall could not be reached.

data.name: ReasonBlockNoExecutable
data.value: There is no program at that path, so there is nothing to block.

data.name: ReasonBlockRuleFailed
data.value: Windows Firewall refused the change. The service log has the details.

data.name: ReasonGeoIpNone
data.value: No GeoIP database found. Put GeoLite2-Country.mmdb and GeoLite2-ASN.mmdb in {0} to see countries and network operators. Keyhole does not download them: they are MaxMind's and need a free account.

data.name: ReasonGeoIpNoCountry
data.value: No country database in {0}; add GeoLite2-Country.mmdb to see countries.

data.name: ReasonGeoIpNoAsn
data.value: No ASN database in {0}; add GeoLite2-ASN.mmdb to see network operators.

data.name: ReasonRecordingNoAdapter
data.value: no packets: no capture adapter could be opened

data.name: ReasonRecordingFileError
data.value: no packets: the capture file could not be created

data.name: ReasonRecordingSizeLimit
data.value: recording stopped at the size limit

data.name: ReasonRecordingSecretsNotEmbedded
data.value: the TLS keys are in the keylog beside the capture, not inside it

data.name: ReasonDecodeNoCapture
data.value: This session recorded no packets, so there is nothing to decode. Packet recording needs Npcap.

data.name: ReasonDecodeUnreadable
data.value: The capture file could not be read.

data.name: ReasonDecodeTooMany
data.value: The capture holds more connections than can be decoded at once; only the first were read.

data.name: ReasonDecodeFailed
data.value: The capture could not be decoded.

data.name: ReasonExchangeResponseTruncated
data.value: the response was still arriving when the capture ended

data.name: ReasonExchangeBodyTruncated
data.value: the body was cut off when the capture ended

data.name: ReasonExchangeHeadersBroken
data.value: the headers could not be decompressed

data.name: ReasonCaptureNoExecutable
data.value: There is no program at that path.

data.name: ReasonCaptureLaunchFailed
data.value: The application could not be started.

data.name: NpcapMissing
data.value: Npcap is not installed, so Keyhole cannot record packets. TLS key logging works without it.

data.name: NpcapStopped
data.value: Npcap is installed but its driver is not running. Start the 'npcap' service to record packets.

data.name: NpcapUnusable
data.value: Npcap is installed but its library could not be found. Reinstalling Npcap should restore it.

data.name: KeylogUnlikely
data.value: uses Windows TLS, which ignores SSLKEYLOGFILE

data.name: KeylogNoneYet
data.value: no keys yet — may use Windows TLS

data.name: DecodeNoneDecrypted
data.value: none of {0} connections could be decrypted

data.name: DecodeNoKeys
data.value: {0} had no key in the capture (these use Windows' own TLS, which ignores SSLKEYLOGFILE)

data.name: DecodeNoHandshake
data.value: {0} had no handshake in the capture, so nothing identified them (either they predate the recording or their first packets were missed)

data.name: DecodeFailedCount
data.value: {0} had a key that Keyhole could not use

data.name: DecodeQuic
data.value: {0} KB of QUIC/HTTP3 was recorded but cannot be decoded

data.name: DecodeNoAnswer
data.value: The service did not finish decoding this capture.

data.name: ActionNoPath
data.value: This entry has no readable executable path, so it cannot be blocked.

data.name: ActionBlockFailed
data.value: The service did not respond; nothing was blocked.

data.name: ActionUnblockFailed
data.value: The service did not respond; the rule was not removed.

data.name: ActionCaptureStartFailed
data.value: The service did not respond; nothing was started.

data.name: ActionCaptureStopFailed
data.value: The service did not respond; the capture was not stopped.

data.name: ActionCaptureStartedSchannel
data.value: Started {0}, but it uses Windows' TLS stack, which ignores SSLKEYLOGFILE. No keys will be written.

data.name: ActionCaptureStartedUnknown
data.value: Started {0}. If the keylog stays at zero bytes, this application uses Windows' TLS stack and cannot be captured this way.

data.name: ActionCaptureStopped
data.value: Stopped capturing {0}. The application is still running.

data.name: ActionNoPcap
data.value: This session recorded no packets, so there is nothing to open.

data.name: ActionOpenedInWireshark
data.value: Opened in Wireshark. The TLS keys are inside the capture, so it decrypts itself.

data.name: ActionOpenedInWiresharkNoKeys
data.value: Opened in Wireshark. This session wrote no TLS keys, so the traffic stays encrypted.

data.name: ActionStartupFailed
data.value: Could not update the sign-in startup entry.

data.name: NpcapInstallerRunning
data.value: Npcap's installer is running. Captures will record packets once it finishes — no need to restart Keyhole.

data.name: NpcapInstallerNotStarted
data.value: The Npcap installer was downloaded and verified but not started. Run it yourself from {0}, or install from {1}.

data.name: NpcapFetchFailed
data.value: Could not fetch Npcap ({0}). Install it from {1}.
